disclosure: Reviewed, source-bound research explanations. These are authored summaries, not live language-model generation or historical quotations. They are invalidated when the underlying page text changes.

llms-and-cognitive-load.mechanism: Imagine asking for roadside help while already stressed. This project tests how a chatbot's role and presentation should adapt to that mental workload.
llms-and-cognitive-load.finding: The project page states a hypothesis: simpler chatbot role cues may help when people are overloaded. It does not present that hypothesis as an established result.

delegating-to-agentic-ai.mechanism: The question is when we let AI choose for us. The study tests whether explaining an AI's insurance recommendations changes people's willingness to delegate the purchase.
delegating-to-agentic-ai.finding: The work is ongoing. It aims to test whether particular explanations encourage delegation even when the recommended insurance product is objectively worse.

genai-in-vr.mechanism: You describe a scene; the system creates a virtual setting. The research asks whether that personal control can improve relaxation.
genai-in-vr.finding: Personalized scene generation is implemented. Improved relaxation, control, engagement and immersion are listed as expected outcomes on the project page, not established findings there.

emg-for-relaxation.mechanism: Sensors detect tension in the neck and shoulder muscle. A virtual-reality exercise then guides relaxation and shows people how their bodily state is changing.
emg-for-relaxation.finding: The project expects sensor-informed virtual relaxation to outperform environments without this feedback. That benefit is an expectation, not a reported result on this page.

human-robot-interaction.mechanism: Robotic training need not ignore the person using it. This project combines physiological signals with emotion classification to display feedback about stress, focus and fatigue.
human-robot-interaction.finding: Better resilience, focus and skill acquisition are expected outcomes. The project page does not establish that adaptive feedback has already delivered those improvements.

neurofeedback-for-relaxation.mechanism: The project brings brain-activity feedback into everyday mental training. It explores wireless EEG, virtual reality and personalized learning for focus and relaxation.
neurofeedback-for-relaxation.finding: Personalized training and a validated virtual-reality protocol are intended outcomes. They should not be mistaken for completed validation simply because the project describes them.

neuromarkers-for-emotion.mechanism: Emotionally demanding conversations consume mental resources. This work studies how customer communication affects cognitive load, wellbeing and performance, and looks for brain-based indicators of those states.
neuromarkers-for-emotion.finding: The work aims to inform real-time support for excessive cognitive load and stress. The listed outcomes are expectations, not established effects of a deployed intervention.

neuromarkers-for-cognitive-load.mechanism: The project uses EEG signals to distinguish levels of mental workload. Its page reports classification into three categories with 60 percent accuracy.
neuromarkers-for-cognitive-load.finding: The page reports 60 percent accuracy across three cognitive-load categories and a result above its baseline classifiers. It does not provide enough detail there for an independent comparison.

llms-for-smes.mechanism: A small business needs more than an impressive model. This project studies conversational recommendations while balancing answer quality, running costs and response time.
llms-for-smes.finding: Prompt-based recommendations were feasible, but costs and latency limited the system to higher-margin settings. An additional retrieval language model was a major contributor to those costs.

telematics-for-road-safety.mechanism: Young drivers receive feedback about their driving. The project studies which kinds of feedback fit different drivers and whether that changes real-world driving behaviour.
telematics-for-road-safety.finding: The reported effect on driving behaviour was small. The effect on accident probability was not statistically significant, so this is not evidence of a proven reduction in accidents.

ar-for-collaboration.mechanism: People with different backgrounds learn data science together in an immersive environment. They build and discuss models rather than encountering only abstract mathematical explanations.
ar-for-collaboration.finding: The system supported sustained collaboration across backgrounds. Clear roles helped, and the researchers emphasized critical thinking rather than blind confidence in model outputs.

ai-for-trust.mechanism: Trust is not simply agreement with a machine. This project examines how people evaluate AI and how decision-support design affects their judgement.
ai-for-trust.finding: In the reported decision-support experiment, recommendations encouraged more uncritical acceptance. Hypothesis-driven support encouraged analytical thinking and better decision accuracy.

transformers-for-emotion-recognition.mechanism: Recognizing emotion takes more than spotting emotional words. This project puts appraisal theory into a transformer to model the context and cognitive processes behind conversational emotions.
transformers-for-emotion-recognition.finding: The project page reports strong benchmark results, including improvements over prior models. The page alone does not establish performance outside the evaluated datasets.

vr-for-relaxation.mechanism: People practice slow, paced breathing while seeing their heart activity in virtual reality. The feedback is intended to support control over stress-related bodily processes.
vr-for-relaxation.finding: The page reports reduced perceived stress after one session. A four-week programme also improved physiological and psychological stress measures compared with a group receiving no intervention.

ai-for-stress-detection.mechanism: Everyday mouse movements, typing and heart activity can provide signals about stress. This project studies detection alongside employees' privacy, accountability and wellbeing concerns.
ai-for-stress-detection.finding: The page reports detecting self-reported stress in a laboratory study. It separately describes real-office validation, so laboratory detection should not be equated with proven workplace deployment.

xai-in-dialog-sentiment.mechanism: DialogueTraX aims to recognize emotion using the surrounding conversation, then explain its predictions. The goal is to make the model's reasoning easier to inspect and debug.
xai-in-dialog-sentiment.finding: Improved accuracy, trust and adaptability are expected outcomes in this project description. The page does not establish that each intended benefit has already been demonstrated.

chatbot-for-trust.mechanism: The project studies roadside-assistance chatbots. It asks how the chatbot's role cues should fit the mental workload people experience while seeking help.
chatbot-for-trust.finding: The page reports that low-complexity role cues suit high-load situations, while richer cues suit simpler settings. That result belongs to this completed chatbot study.

ai-investment-agent.mechanism: The project combines language-model signals with reinforcement learning for stock trading. It studies whether textual market information can improve the trading framework.
ai-investment-agent.finding: The reported improvements come from backtests on market data. They are not evidence of guaranteed future returns or a verified live-trading advantage.
